newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke back-pedals over Europe - Express.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke back-pedals over Europe - Express.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke has made a "dramatic New Year's resolution" -- to build bridges to his anti-European critics, The Express newspaper reported on Wednesday.
The paper said Clarke planned a series of meetings to reassure anti-European rightwingers in the ruling Conservative Party that he is not hell-bent on rushing into a single European currency.
Clarke wanted to defuse the civil war within the party and to stop it falling apart ahead of the general election, which Prime Minister John Major must call by next May.
The Express quoted friends of the chancellor as saying he wanted to damp down a row that erupted two weeks ago after his off-the-record remarks were quoted by journalists.

Clarke, a pro-European, was quoted as saying then that attempts by Major to toughen cabinet opposition to the single European currency were a "boomerang" that had blown up in the prime minister's face.

One of Clarke's allies was quoted by The Express as saying: "He wants to show that he is not the devil incarnate, that there is no conspiracy to sign up for the single currency by the back door and that -- in prvate -- he is also highly doubtful that Britain will enter economic and monetary union in the next parliament.
"Ken was badly shaken by the events of two weeks ago and he accepts he was partly at fault.
"He knows the party stared into the abyss during that row and he wants to do all he can to stop it tearing itself apart over Europe in the run-up to the election."
Following a by-election victory by the opposition Labour Party, Major now has no majority in the lower House of Commons.
